subject: frog
pitch: A red-eyed tree frog clinging to a leaf. Vivid lime-green skin, blue and cream striped flanks, orange toes with round sticky pads, a creamy white belly, and enormous ruby-red eyes with black slit pupils. It looks a little surprised, as if you just woke it up.
reasoning:
I need to work out the correct SDK API usage from the reference docs—functions like creating a builder, defining joints, chains, sweeps, parts, and sticks with their proper parameters.

There's also a long tail of other API surface (surface hits, decals, regions, rings, procedural paint patterns like stripes and spots, geometry helpers like bezier and catmull curves) that I should avoid relying on too heavily since their exact signatures are uncertain, risking runtime errors. I'll stick to the well-documented basics—builder, joint, part, stick, sweep—and keep the frog's design simple and stylized, using scale within part options to shape a squat body rather than reaching for riskier undocumented calls.

For pose, I'm imagining a frog clinging to a leaf, with the leaf itself as a simple tilted prop whose lowest point touches y=0, built from a flattened and rotated sphere or box rather than anything geometrically complex.

Since nothing can hang below y=0, I'll anchor the leaf so its lowest point touches the ground, centering it around y=0.35 with semi-axes roughly 0.25 by 0.35, and keep the frog scaled for readability at about 0.1m rather than true-to-life size. For the pose, I'm picturing the frog hunched upright facing forward, clinging to the leaf with legs folded and toe pads gripping the surface, built from scaled ellipsoid shapes for the body.

Now I'm working out the joint hierarchy -- a hip/body root, a neck-to-head chain, and leg chains with hip, knee, ankle, and foot joints positioned so the thighs splay outward and the shins curl back to plant the feet near the leaf's surface, adjusting the leaf's z-depth slightly so the feet appear to actually touch rather than float.

I'm also figuring out how to build the limb geometry itself -- whether to use capsule/rod primitives between points directly or construct proper chains with b.chain so the legs are riggable, since sweeping a chain with a radius seems like the safer, more consistent approach than guessing at capsule parameters.

To minimize risk, I'll lean on b.part with known three.js geometries and b.joint for skeleton structure, letting auto bone-assignment handle attachment, and reserve b.chain mainly for cases like the legs where a defined role actually matters.

I'll keep legs simple with chains swept at constant radius plus toe pad spheres. For the face, I'm placing red eye spheres on the head sides with flattened black pupil slits offset slightly forward, and for the body I'm shaping a lime sphere with scale adjustments, adding a cream belly patch, and considering thin torus arcs for flank stripes.

Rotating tori is awkward without an aim direction, so I'll skip that and instead use small scaled boxes positioned along the flanks at increasing heights to form blue and cream stripe bands, approximating their placement on the ellipsoid surface. Toes get small orange sphere tips with flattened pad discs near the foot points, and the head will be a flattened variant of the main body sphere.

Now I'm working out the leaf shape as a flattened sphere stretched to an oval disc, with a dark green midrib box on its front face, and positioning the frog's body center and feet above the leaf surface so the proportions line up correctly in the z-depth.

Shifting the body position so its back edge sits flush against the leaf front, then placing the hip, knee, ankle, and foot joints for each leg with small toe pad spheres at the foot tips, all connected through chain and sweep calls to build lime-colored tube limbs with orange pads.

I'm now working through how joints should parent to each other, planning a root "hips" joint at the body center with a child "head" joint positioned forward and up, while assuming the chain calls will auto-attach their first points to the nearest existing joint.

To minimize risk I'll limit explicit joints to the root plus maybe one child, and add a few deterministic darker-green spot details on the back using a seeded random function for placement, assuming it returns values in [0,1).

Now I'm working through precise eye and pupil geometry so the pupils actually sit visibly on the eye surface rather than being hidden inside the sphere, adjusting the z-offsets until the pupil protrudes slightly past the eye front.

Then I'm sketching the highlight dot for a glossy look, and starting to think through how to add flank stripes using boxes, running into the issue of not having clean rotation control for angling them along the body.

For the stripe placement, I'm computing the body's cross-sectional half-width at a given height using the ellipsoid's curvature formula, then positioning each stripe box just inside that boundary so it hugs the surface reasonably well despite the simplification. I'm also working out a cream-colored belly patch as a flattened sphere nestled into the front-lower body, adjusting its position and scale so it reads as a belly marking rather than poking out oddly.

For the back, I'm scattering a batch of dark spots using spherical coordinates mapped onto the body ellipsoid, filtering so they land only on the upper-back region and flattening each one slightly so it looks like a surface marking rather than a bump.

I'm building out the feet with a fan of small toe pads at each foot and hand tip, using angle-based offsets to spread them, plus a simple mouth line, nostril dots, and a leaf perch with a midrib detail, all while tuning z-offsets so the feet, belly, and leaf surfaces sit close together without obvious gaps or overlaps. Finally I'm sketching the actual build function — defining joints, body/limb geometry, chains for the legs and arms with sweep-based limb meshes, toe pad fans, eye spheres with pupils and highlights, and stripe/spot placement using the halfX helper — all pulled together into one exported builder function.
